context: Table S4: no detectable DON in the Sdh deletion mutants (free-living, in vitro). Closest existing term is PHIPO:0001445 'decreased'; PHIPO:0000234 'absent' is within-host, so wrong context for an in-vitro assay.

Figure 7A: ABC1 transcript strongly induced by the rice phytoalexin sakuranetin (40 ug/ml, 5 h). The host-derived inducer is the whole point of the efflux-pump-as-defence hypothesis. Sibling set fixes every field: PECO:0005181 + miconazole, PECO:0005326 + metconazole, PECO:0005050 + hygromycin B, PECO:0000257 + cycloheximide.

Figure 6 / Table I barley penetration assay is scored at 60 h. PECO's dpi series runs 2,3,5,6,7 days and its hours series stops well short of 60. Rounding to PECO:0005226 '2 days' misstates it by 12 h at the stage where wild type goes from appressorium to a filled cell, so the timing was left unmapped.

Table II drug panel. PHIPO's 'normal growth on X' branch has ~60 siblings (e.g. PHIPO:0001309 benomyl, PHIPO:0001428 brefeldin A, PHIPO:0001393 metconazole) but none for miconazole, propiconazole, fenarimol, chloramphenicol, cycloheximide, fenpropimorph, 4-NQO or sakuranetin — 8 of the 13 compounds tested. NOTE: annotations parked anyway because Table II shows no per-strain data (see draft flag #3); this is a term-coverage gap, not a request to annotate this paper.

Table I: conidial attachment to plastic coverslips, 90/92/82 per cent, unremarkable. PHIPO:0000184 'pathogen adhesion to host phenotype' is OBSOLETE with no replacement. Note the assay uses an inert surface, not host tissue, so a revived host-adhesion term might still not apply.
phrase: normal spore attachment to an artificial surface
